byCritic.checked: Full surface of app/src (model, constraints, io/{parseRoster,importGraph,exportGraph,clamp,feasibility,download,readFileText,schema,constraintMessages}, worker/{generate,protocol}, state/*, graph/{layout,highlight,GraphCanvas}, search, neighborhood, panels/*, App) plus the lib functions they consume. Reproduced with probes under .review-scratch/critic-correctness-app/: (1) 3000-graph import fuzz asserting aspl-null/quality-0/caption/optimality/buddy-symmetry/degree-extent/export-idempotence invariants — all held; (2) 400 constrained generations checking constraintSummary against the actual edge set and metrics.connected against report.connected — 0 disagreements; (3) 600-graph check that diameter === max eccentricity, that shortest paths have no chords (validating edgeClass's route-membership proof), and that disconnected graphs report null diameter; (4) 4000-case hostile-character fuzz proving parseRoster idempotence and that every roster it emits is accepted by importGraph; (5) seed-pair scans (~600 buildBuddyGraph pairs) looking for set-equal/order-different edge lists to break useBuddyGraph.sameEdges — none, and traced Graph.edgeList() to be canonical+sorted, so the positional comparison is provably a set comparison; (6) traced all four degenerate branches of mooreLowerBounds to confirm the app's quality()/assembleMetrics gates cover every asplGap===0 sentinel; (7) confirmed degreeMax never exceeds k for any generatable (n,k), so a generated graph can never be refused by importGraph's per-vertex degree gate; (8) confirmed d3-force v3 draws jiggle randomness from a per-simulation lcg, so forceLayout is deterministic, and that no Math.random/Date.now exists in app/src. app npm test green (270 passed) before and after.

Full-surface adversarial DoS/injection pass over app/src (all 30 source files plus app/test), with executable probes under app/.review-scratch/ (gitignored, outside the pinned test/** vitest glob).

GATE ORDERING (traced statically, io/importGraph.ts): every size/shape gate precedes the work it bounds — people.length > MAX_IMPORT_N before people.map; 2m <= BUDDY_MAX*n density gate before the per-edge loop and new Graph; declaredPairs > MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS before any per-pair work and before validate's O(n^2) walk could ever be reached; per-name MAX_NAME_CHARS before any message interpolates a name; per-vertex degreeMax > BUDDY_MAX before the O(n^2) allPairsSummary/girth; joined-length check before the parseRoster round-trip. readFileText's byte gate precedes the read and therefore JSON.parse.

MEASURED main-thread worst cases: maximal legal import (n=1000, 12-regular, 6000 edges) 78 ms through importGraph; long-diameter path-graph variant 64 ms; allPairsSummary 71 ms, girth 4-38 ms. forceLayout(1000,6000) 233 ms, flat across n=120/400/1000 (152/175/233 ms) via forceIters scaling. parseRoster at the 500K char cap across six pathological shapes (all-dupes 1- and 2-char tokens, all-blank, all-over-length, one 500K token, all-distinct) peaks at 44 ms; MAX_NAMES early break and char cap both hold. rankMatches with a 200-char query (the input's maxLength) vs 1000 x 120-char names 5.6 ms. validateDetailed at n=1000 with 200 prohibited pairs (the O(n^2) connectivity walk reachable per keystroke via RosterModal's ruleProblems memo) 3.5 ms.

FUZZ: 40,000 randomized hostile importGraph inputs (atoms incl. -0, 1e308, 2**53, 0.5, tab, 400-char strings, wrong-shaped constraints/settings/people/edges, __proto__ injection) — zero non-ImportError escapes, worst single call 1.84 ms, no prototype pollution.

SPREADSHEET/CLIPBOARD SINK: imported names "=HYPERLINK(1)" and "+b" (they pass every gate) and followed them to both sinks. toCsv neutralizes per cell before quote-doubling; every character that could act as a CSV field/row delimiter (comma, \n, \r, \t, U+2028/2029) is refused by importGraph's NAME_HOSTILE_CHARS test or the parseRoster round-trip check, and normalized to spaces on the roster path — so no cell can contain an embedded delimiter to split on. BuddyList.copyAll neutralizes only the line-leading name, but the clipboard sink's delimiters are tab and newline, both refused in names, so every line is exactly one cell and the leading-character guard covers the whole surface. The "; " and ", " joins are not delimiters of either sink.

NUMERIC EDGES: -0 seed clamps to 0; 1e999 (Infinity) minSeparation falls back to SEPARATION_DEFAULT; non-integer edge endpoints refused; Set normalizes -0 endpoints; exportGraph writes only finiteOrNull-normalized metrics and clamped settings, so JSON.stringify has no Infinity to convert.

themes.theme: Name truncation splits a UTF-16 surrogate pair, producing an ill-formed string that different serializers (JSON vs UTF-8 CSV) resolve differently, so the displayed name and the exported name silently diverge
findingSummaries: parseRoster truncates over-long names with String.slice (a UTF-16 code-unit boundary). A name whose MAX_NAME_CHARS-th unit is the high half of a surrogate pair is emitted as an ill-formed string with a trailing lone surrogate. This passes importGraph's control-char gate and its idempotency/round-trip check, then diverges downstream: JSON.stringify escapes the lone surrogate (round-trips fine), but downloadBlob/toCsv's UTF-8 encoding replaces it with U+FFFD — so the organizer's CSV shows a different name than the buddy list on screen.
themes.remediation: Stop truncating by code unit: cut the trailing lone surrogate off the slice result (or slice on an Array.from code-point array) so parseRoster can never emit an ill-formed string in the first place — this removes the divergence at its single source rather than reconciling it at each sink.

themes.theme: Docstrings still name the pre-refactor worker result type, no longer matching the normalized type the code actually receives
findingSummaries: model.ts docstring refers to BuddyResult but the function parameter is GraphResult.
useBuddyGraph.ts docstring says the code 'maps its BuddyResult back' but it actually receives GraphResult from the worker protocol.
themes.remediation: Delete the stale BuddyResult references from both comments and state once, in whichever file is canonical for the worker-protocol type, that GraphResult is the normalized outcome of the core's BuddyResult/ConstrainedBuddyResult builders — removing the second, drifted description rather than maintaining two independent explanations of the same type.

themes.theme: A live-region announcement is placed inside an `inert` subtree in the same commit that gives it its text, so assistive tech never hears it — and the code's own comment claims otherwise only because one path happens to duplicate the message elsewhere by coincidence
findingSummaries: When first-time generation fails at the worker level, the effect calls show(bg.error) and setModalOpen(true) in the same commit; the Notice's role="status" region sits inside a div that goes inert=false→true in that same commit, so it's excluded from the accessibility tree exactly when it receives its only text. The refused-constraints path happens to duplicate the same message inside RosterModal's own non-inert note stack, masking the bug there, but the worker-error path has no such duplicate — leaving a screen-reader user in a silently reopened, unexplained dialog on every retry. The adjacent code comment asserting 'the message is announced by its own role="status"' is false for this path.
themes.remediation: Remove the coupling that makes Notice inert in the same commit it receives text: stop wrapping the Notice in the modalOpen-driven inert container (exclude it from that wrapper, or drop the inert={modalOpen} toggle on it) so the region is never hidden by a same-commit ancestor change, rather than adding a second announcement channel for the missing case.

themes.theme: Focus recovery for hidden file-picker triggers depends on a React commit that a canceled native dialog never produces, stranding focus on <body>
findingSummaries: Both hidden file inputs (App.tsx's QualityPanel import button, RosterModal's choose-a-file button) are display:none and opened via ref.current?.click(), with no cancel handler anywhere in the app. useFocusRescue is the sole focus-recovery mechanism and only runs after a React commit; selecting a file fires onChange and a commit, so rescue works, but canceling the picker fires nothing, so focus — which browsers commonly leave on <body> when the trigger is unfocusable display:none — is never rescued, and the very next Tab restarts navigation from the top of the document, the exact failure useFocusRescue exists to prevent.
themes.remediation: Remove the display:none hidden-input pattern that makes the trigger unfocusable — switch both file inputs to visually-hidden-but-focusable styling (position:absolute; 1x1px; overflow:hidden; opacity:0) so the browser's own dialog-close focus restoration covers the cancel case, eliminating the need for a change-event-dependent rescue path for this trigger.

gating.theme: a name is cut mid-character during normalisation, so the name shown on screen is not the name written to the exported file
gating.summary: parseRoster truncates over-long names with String.slice, which counts UTF-16 code units. A name whose MAX_NAME_CHARS-th unit is the high half of a surrogate pair is emitted as an ill-formed UTF-16 string (trailing lone surrogate). It passes every downstream gate — it is not in Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp so importGraph's control-char refusal misses it, and parseRoster is idempotent on it so importGraph's round-trip check accepts it — and then diverges between sinks: JSON.stringify escapes the lone surrogate (so JSON export/import round-trips), but downloadBlob/toCsv encode UTF-8, where a lone surrogate is replaced by U+FFFD. The organizer's CSV therefore contains a different name than the buddy list on screen.
gating.failure: parseRoster("a".repeat(119) + "\u{1F600}" + "tail") emits a 120-unit name ending in the lone high surrogate 0xD83D; String.prototype.isWellFormed() === false. new TextDecoder().decode(new TextEncoder().encode(toCsv([[name]]))) !== toCsv([[name]]) — the exported CSV cell ends in U+FFFD while BuddyList/Slips render the surrogate. The name is also accepted unchanged by importGraph, so the ill-formed value is durable in the app's own file format. test/parseRoster.test.ts:111 truncates only "x".repeat(...), so the existing suite cannot observe this.
gating.remediation: Truncate by code point rather than code unit — e.g. `const cut = Array.from(raw); const token = cut.length > MAX_NAME_CHARS ? cut.slice(0, MAX_NAME_CHARS).join("").trim() : raw;` — or, minimally, drop a trailing lone surrogate after slicing. Ratchet with a property test over parseRoster's whole output: every emitted name satisfies isWellFormed(). Consider applying the same well-formedness predicate in importGraph's name gate, since a hand-edited file can supply a lone surrogate directly and reach the same CSV sink.
gating.invariant: For every input string s, every name in parseRoster(s).names is well-formed UTF-16 (String.prototype.isWellFormed() === true), i.e. contains no unpaired surrogate — equivalently, new TextDecoder().decode(new TextEncoder().encode(name)) === name for every emitted name.

gating.theme: Documentation names a type the function no longer receives; stale after refactoring to normalize worker results
gating.summary: Docstring refers to BuddyResult but function parameter is GraphResult
gating.failure: The viewFromResult function (line 397) accepts `r: GraphResult`, not `BuddyResult`. The comment on line 389 states 'Combine a worker BuddyResult' but BuddyResult is the intermediate type in the worker; GraphResult is what crosses the boundary. When a new contributor reads this comment while reading the function signature, the two do not match.
gating.invariant: Every docstring that names a specific type must match the actual parameter types: if a docstring names `BuddyResult`, the function signature must have `BuddyResult` in the parameter list, not `GraphResult`
gating.remediation: Update line 389 to: 'Combine a worker GraphResult (normalized from BuddyResult or ConstrainedBuddyResult) with the roster + settings into a GraphView.' This reflects that GraphResult is the actual type received, and acknowledges it's normalized from the core's two builder types.

gating.theme: Documentation describes flow using a type name that was normalized away; stale after worker protocol refactoring
gating.summary: Docstring says 'maps its BuddyResult back' but receives GraphResult from worker protocol
gating.failure: useBuddyGraph receives `gen.result` which is typed as `GraphResult` (from the worker protocol), not `BuddyResult`. The hook's own docstring on line 18 says 'maps its BuddyResult back into a GraphView'. A contributor reading the docstring, then tracing to the worker protocol (protocol.ts), would find `GraphResult` defined there, creating a search-and-trace mismatch that looks like an error.
gating.invariant: Documentation describing data flow must match the actual types in the implementation: if a docstring names BuddyResult as input, the implementation must show BuddyResult flowing in, not GraphResult
gating.remediation: Update line 18-19 to: 'Orchestrates generation: sends a job to the worker and maps its GraphResult (a normalized builder outcome) back into a GraphView using the exact roster + settings that produced it.' This clarifies that GraphResult is what the worker protocol carries, normalized from the core's actual builder result types.

gating.theme: an aria-live explanation is wrapped in `inert` in the exact same commit that gives it its text, so assistive tech never sees it
gating.summary:
When a first-time generation fails at the worker level (`bg.status === "error"`, e.g. the worker script fails to load/parse — the exact case `useGenerationWorker.ts`'s own `onerror`/`onmessageerror` handlers were added to catch), the effect at App.tsx:150-166 calls `show(bg.error || "Generation failed.")` and `setModalOpen(true)` together, synchronously, inside one effect body. React 18/19 batches both into a single commit. In that same commit, `
` (App.tsx:427-429) goes straight from `(inert=false, message=null)` to `(inert=true, message=text)`. Per spec, an `inert` subtree is excluded from the accessibility tree, so the `role="status"` region inside it is never exposed to assistive technology at the moment it receives its only text — the announcement that explains why the dialog silently reopened. Unlike the constraint-refusal path (`bg.status==="refused"`), where `RosterModal`'s own internal note stack happens to recompute the identical blocking message from the same `validateDetailed` predicate and thereby duplicates the toast's content in a non-inert region, the worker-error path has no such duplicate: the modal's own feasibility/rule checks say nothing about "Generation failed to start" or "Generation sent back something unreadable". A screen-reader user is left in a dialog that looks freshly opened, with an enabled "Generate buddy graph" button, zero explanation of what happened, and — because retrying reproduces the same worker failure the same way — a silent loop: each retry regenerates the same unannounced toast. The code comment at App.tsx:421-426 explicitly asserts "Nothing is lost: the message is announced by its own role=\"status\"", which is false for exactly this path; the claim is only true today for the refused-constraints path, and only by coincidence of two independent code paths (worker validateDetailed vs. RosterModal's own validateDetailed) computing the same string, not by the toast itself being reachable.
gating.failure: Cold load -> paste a valid roster -> click "Generate buddy graph" while the generation worker fails to start (e.g. blocked script, corrupted deploy, a browser extension interfering with module workers) -> bg.status becomes "error" -> show(bg.error) + setModalOpen(true) fire in one commit -> the toast's role=status region is rendered already-inert with its first (and only) text -> a screen-reader user hears nothing, sees the roster dialog reopened with no stated reason, and gets no accessible signal to explain or work around the failure.
gating.remediation: Never pair `show()`/`flash()` with `setModalOpen(true)` in the same commit. Either (a) defer setting `modalOpen` by one tick/render (e.g. via a second effect keyed on `notice`) so the toast is announced in a non-inert state before its ancestor becomes inert, or (b) duplicate the message inside RosterModal's own always-mounted, non-inert `role="status"` note stack (the way the refused-constraints path already does by accident) — pass the reopening reason in as a prop and render it there unconditionally, not only for the constraint-refusal subset.
gating.invariant: For any two states S0 -> S1 committed together where S0 had `notice === null` and S1 has both `notice !== null` and `modalOpen === true` (making the toast's wrapper `inert`), the same text must also be reachable through some `role="status"`/`aria-live` region that is NOT a descendant of an `inert` element in S1. Equivalently: no `aria-live` region's first-ever appearance of a given message may occur inside a subtree whose `inert` attribute is `true` in that same render.

plausible.theme: focus recovery after a removed/blurred element relies on a React commit that a canceled native file-picker never produces
plausible.summary: Both file-import affordances (`app/src/App.tsx:409-419`'s hidden `<input type="file">` behind QualityPanel's "Import ↑" button, and `app/src/panels/RosterModal.tsx:133-143`'s hidden input behind "choose a file") are `display:none` and are opened via `ref.current?.click()`. Neither has an `onCancel` handler, and a repo-wide grep confirms no `cancel` event listener exists anywhere in `app/src`. `useFocusRescue` (app/src/state/useFocusRescue.ts) is the app's ONLY mechanism for recovering focus that lands on `<body>`, and by its own design it runs its rescue effect "after EVERY commit" — i.e. it depends on a React re-render happening at all. Selecting a file fires `onChange`, which drives a state update (`setRoster`/`handleImportFile`) that produces a commit, so the rescue engages correctly on that path (traced and consistent with the surrounding code's extensive, well-documented handling of the analogous "unmount removes focus" cases). But dismissing the native file-picker WITHOUT choosing a file fires no `change` event and therefore no React commit at all — so even if `hadFocus.current` is `true`, the rescue effect never re-runs to catch it. `display:none` elements are unfocusable per spec, so the hidden input itself cannot become `document.activeElement`; browsers commonly leave `document.activeElement` on `<body>` in this scenario once the native dialog closes over an unfocusable trigger (a widely-documented pattern, which is exactly why other apps use visually-hidden-but-focusable inputs instead of `display:none` for this). With `#app` not inert at this point (a graph exists, the modal is closed), a body-stranded focus means the very next Tab press restarts navigation from the top of the entire document — precisely the failure `useFocusRescue`'s own doc comment says the mechanism exists to prevent ("the next Tab restarts at the top of the document").
